chapter: Band personalities, Duke's last years and the office
title: On the road with Pearl Bailey and Louie Bellson, and refusing to manage
summary: Louie wanted him as manager; he went as a trombonist, then quit after friction with the other trombonist.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I worked with Pearl Bailey and the band on the road with Louie.

He worked in that band. Louie wanted Juan to be manager, and Juan turned him down. And then they were in Las Vegas, and they sent for us to come to Las Vegas, that they wanted to see us. So we went to Las Vegas and spent the weekend, and I think Pearl was working at the
Flamingo, and they gave her a little house to stay in and everything right across from the Flamingo, and of course, we stayed there in the house with them.

And Louie talked Juan in to coming into the band. But Juan didn't go as manager; he only went as a trombone player. But he called Juan in Las Vegas; he called Juan and wanted Juan to be the manager. So I said to Juan, I said, 'Why don't you take it?' and he said, 'Oh, I don't want to go'. I guess Juan was just tired of the road, you know?

I traveled so much on busses, until I told Pearl, you give me a ticket for the train; I didn't want to travel on busses any more. And since then, Rose, I believe that's the reason why Pearl didn't have too much to do with me then, because I refused, and let her spend a lot of money for railroad fare for me, while the band was traveling on the bus, and I said, 'I want my train -- I don't like busses' -- I did that just too much.

Even when we were in Washington with the show, and the next stop was Las Vegas, they asked me, 'How about it? You going with us to the plane to Las Vegas?' I said, 'No, give me a train.' So I took the train from Washington to Las Vegas. Since that time, they're not like they used to be.

Louie was all right, and then, like when we were at the hotel here, the Ambassador -- the Hotel Ambassador here, they want for me to work for so and so and I want so and so and so. I said no. And every payday, Louie had to go to the cashier and give me my money, because what's his name was the manager then, the other trombone player ...

Yeah, I think he was a little jealous of Juan. Because, see, Louie asked Juan to be manager, and Juan told him he didn't want that -- because you know, you make a lot of enemies being the manager, and Juan said, 'I don't want to be the manager of no band.' Juan used to start Duke Ellington's band for him all the time for him, you know, rehearsing, and he did the same thing for Harry James, and you know, you make a lot of enemies like that.
So Juan said he didn't want to be the manager, so when Louie told Juan that he'd give him some extra money if he would stay, Juan said no. So Juan left.
Well, that's about all, I guess.
